source.scope: Primary genetic study of 18 free-living putative Callithrix hybrids captured during 2004-2013 at Biritiba Mirim (Sao Paulo) and Guapimirim, Teresopolis/PARNASO, and Petropolis (Rio de Janeiro), within southeastern Brazil's Atlantic Forest. The paper compares maternally inherited COX2 haplotypes and paternal SRY markers; it also used 15 positive-control animals. The five HCj observations are among the putative hybrid samples, not a representative sample of pure C. jacchus populations.

claims.text: Among 18 free-living putative marmoset hybrids sampled at four southeastern Brazilian localities during 2004-2013, the study identified the C. jacchus COX2 haplotype HCj in five individuals (Csp1-2 from Biritiba Mirim in 2004 and Csp9-11 from Nogueira in 2012). The paper discusses hybridization between native threatened C. aurita and introduced congeners including C. jacchus as a conservation concern. These mitochondrial observations document a C. jacchus maternal lineage in this sample; they do not estimate hybridization frequency in C. jacchus, quantify demographic impact, or establish this species' conservation status or population trend.
claims.textZh: 在 2004–2013 年于巴西东南部四个地点采集的 18 只自由活动、外形疑似杂交的绒猴中，研究在 5 只个体（2004 年 Biritiba Mirim 的 Csp1–2，以及 2012 年 Nogueira 的 Csp9–11）检出归属于普通绒猴（C. jacchus）的 COX2 单倍型 HCj。论文将原生受威胁种 C. aurita 与包括普通绒猴在内的外来近缘种之间的杂交列为保育关注。该线粒体观察只记录了这一样本中的普通绒猴母系标记；它没有估计普通绒猴的杂交频率、量化种群影响，也没有确定该物种的保育状态或种群趋势。
claims.locator: Results, Sample data and COX2 analysis (18 free-living putative hybrids; five HCj samples); Table 1 and Fig. 1 (sample IDs, localities, capture years); Discussion (hybridization context and limitations of uniparental markers).
claims.placeTimeScope: Four Atlantic Forest localities in southeastern Brazil: Biritiba Mirim, Sao Paulo; Guapimirim, Teresopolis/PARNASO, and Petropolis, Rio de Janeiro. The 18 putative hybrid individuals were captured from 2004 through 2013; the five HCj records were from Biritiba Mirim in 2004 and Nogueira in 2012.
claims.lifeStatus: The relevant observations concern free-living putative hybrids with mixed phenotypes, not a representative sample of pure wild C. jacchus individuals; pure-species controls are distinct from the 18 hybrid samples.

conservation: This source documents C. jacchus maternal markers among a bounded sample of free-living putative hybrids in a conservation-relevant interaction with C. aurita. Current C. jacchus assessment status, population trend, the prevalence of such hybridization, and measured demographic or genetic impacts remain unassessed.
